youtube_title: The Eastland, 1915: the picnic boat to Michigan City that never left the dock
body: They were headed for a picnic in Michigan City. On July 24, 1915, Western Electric workers and their families boarded the steamer Eastland in Chicago. About 2,500 people were aboard when, still tied up in the Chicago River, the ship rolled over onto its side. 844 people died, the deadliest shipwreck on the Great Lakes. Today, beside the Old Lighthouse in Michigan City, an anchor chain of 844 links stretches across the grounds, one link for each person who died. In Chicago, people say they still see faces in the river. Michigan City still remembers them.
